gaps.category: Czech Trade Licensing Act (živnostenský zákon) regulated trades: firearms-adjacent and vehicle trades beyond dismantlers, e.g. technical inspection stations (STK), emission stations (SME), tachograph workshops and driving-school registers
gaps.first_search: stanice měření emisí STK povinnosti ISTK hlášení software malé provozovny 2026
gaps.why: Thousands of small family garages must file inspection results to the state vehicle register (CRV/ISTK) and calibrate and report tachograph and emission checks; strict, recurring and state-mandated. Only dismantlers and driving schools were touched, and STK/SME was never screened.

gaps.category: Municipal local-fee and register duties on small operators: místní poplatky, poplatek za komunální odpad, and the new construction-act and waste-law municipal registers (e.g. sběrné dvory, zpětný odběr)
gaps.first_search: povinnosti výrobců a prodejců obalů zpětný odběr hlášení EKO-KOM malé e-shopy 2026 PPWR
gaps.why: Act 541/2020 and the EPR system (extended producer responsibility) put reporting duties on small producers and sellers of packaging, electronics, batteries and tyres via collective schemes (EKO-KOM, ASEKOL, Elektrowin). Small e-shops and importers face growing obligations from 2025-2026 (packaging regulation PPWR), and this was only screened as K11 waste records.

gaps.category: Excise and customs duties on small Czech producers other than distilleries and wine: breweries (minipivovary), cider and mead makers, spirit bottlers, tobacco/hemp (CBD) sellers
gaps.first_search: minipivovar spotřební daň evidence výroby přiznání celní správa software malý pivovar
gaps.why: Czechia has one of the densest micro-brewery and craft-spirit scenes in Europe; they file excise returns to Customs, keep production records and, for small brewers, claim reduced excise rates. K15 rejected only distilleries; minibreweries are not covered at all.

gaps.category: Daňový/ pension and social-security small-business filings: OSVČ annual returns, přehled pro ČSSZ a zdravotní pojišťovny, and new 2026 flat-tax (paušální daň) changes
gaps.first_search: paušální daň 2026 změny OSVČ přehled ČSSZ zdravotní pojišťovna povinnosti software
gaps.why: The largest group of Czech micro-firms are OSVČ (sole traders, about 1 million). Annual overviews to ČSSZ and health insurers, paušální režim thresholds and deadlines, and 2026 changes to the tax-and-insurance regime are a mandatory recurring workflow. It may be crowded (generic accounting), but no coverage row exists and the scoping against generic accounting was not tested.

gaps.category: Housing associations and owner communities: SVJ (společenství vlastníků jednotek) and bytová družstva
gaps.first_search: SVJ povinnosti správa domu evidence skuteční majitelé účetní závěrka výpisy software pro společenství vlastníků
gaps.why: Roughly 50,000+ SVJ and housing co-operatives are small associations with statutory duties: annual accounts, assembly minutes, the Real Beneficial Owners register, energy/heat-cost allocation, lift and gas revisions, electronic register of the Cadastre. Category 17 covered associations and co-operatives 23 only as credit unions; SVJ is a big, Czech-specific population.

gaps.category: New laws 2024-2027 hitting small operators: whistleblower act (zákon 171/2023, 50+ employees; 2026 amendments), accessibility act (zákon 424/2023, EAA from June 2025 for e-shops and microenterprise exemptions), and beneficial-owner register (evidence skutečných majitelů) sanctions
gaps.first_search: evidence skutečných majitelů povinnost zápis spolek firma pokuta 2026 whistleblowing kanál 50 zaměstnanců malé firmy
gaps.why: These are deadlines that make many small firms act at once. EAA/accessibility of e-shops and the whistleblower channel for 50+ staff employers are recent duties not mentioned in the coverage table; evidence skutečných majitelů is a recurring filing duty for associations and companies.

candidates.buyer: Small and family wineries and grape growers (several thousand, mostly South Moravia); no verified count

candidates.name: Wine-grower record books and declarations desk
candidates.trigger: Evidence books (Act 321/2004 Sb., vyhl. 323/2004 Sb.) must be written up by the next working day after grape intake (per NSS ruling citing Reg. 436/2009, which may have been replaced; check). SZPI checks the books and fines errors.
candidates.unchecked: Whether Czech rules allow electronic evidence books; Czech vendors; current Reg. 436/2009 replacement; number of winemakers; SZPI fine levels; 2026 dates.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: One search; nothing found. Only generic employer rules and the 1 Jan 2026 health-insurance change (state-paid category for carers of 2+ children abolished), which affects parents, not people who hire nannies. No household-employer register or filing duty found; not a mass segment in Czechia. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Cash purchases from individuals banned since 2015 (non-cash only); records fall under waste law (ISOH/ISPOP), already rejected as K11. Nothing new beyond K11.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbroking is a free (ohlašovací) trade; the only duty found is ID checks of sellers, from an old, unverified source. No register or periodic report found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: AML duty applies to precious-metal traders (cash of EUR 10,000 or more; report to FAÚ within 5 days) plus puncovní (assay office) supervision under Act 539/1992. No gold-purchase register duty confirmed. Logged as a weak, unverified candidate.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Dismantlers report end-of-life vehicles in the state MA ISOH module (vyhl. 345/2021 Sb.). Intake photos and records appear to be due within about 4 days; this comes from a secondary source and is unverified. A new law with recertification of all dismantlers is planned. No commercial dismantler software found. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Keepers must report births, deaths and movements to the central register within 7 days (vyhl. 136/2004 Sb., amended by 174/2019 Sb.). Reporting is through the free Portál farmáře and ČMSCH. Even a keeper of one sheep counts as a keeper. Logged as rejected: free state tool.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Only found that SVS runs the register of farms and animals. Slaughter-reporting formats and any software were not found. Thin result; the category is not exhausted.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Annual report of colonies by 15 Sept via the free web form eagri.cz/HlaseniVcely (ČMSCH, no account needed). Rejected: free state tool. A 2026 subsidy decree (NV 126/2026 Sb.) is about grants only.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K09 (rejected).

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Organisations doing geological works, including water-well drilling, must register them with the Czech Geological Survey (ČGS) about 30 days before starting and report changes within 30 days. Free portal procedure. Few firms; low pain. Logged as weak.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Since 2021 (Act 544/2020 Sb.) homeowners must prove cesspit emptying for the last 2 years, with hauler-issued proof showing date, volume, site and destination plant. Inspections and fines are stepping up (2026 articles). No haulers' software found. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Regime is Act 250/2021 Sb. (in force 1 Jul 2022; amended by 318/2025 Sb.): operators keep a register of regulated technical equipment (VTZ) and revision schedules. Not checked: competing revision-management tools. Boiler inspector side is K04. Logged as unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Risk assessment and management of drinking-water systems is mandatory (Act 258/2000 Sb., 2023 amendment). The state health institute (SZÚ) publishes a simplified method for small systems (2018). Priority buildings for lead and legionella (schools, nurseries, health and social facilities, some accommodation) come from the EU directive 2020/2184. 2026 deadlines not confirmed. Logged as unverified.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Registered distributors (ÚKZÚZ register) must keep running receipt and issue records, check the professional certificate at sale, and pass storage inspections. Applicator records are K08 (rejected). Distributor side logged as weak.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: The agency-employment deposit of CZK 500,000 and insolvency insurance date from 2017. Since 1 Apr 2026, hiring foreigners is reported only through JMHZ/REGZEC, which is K10. No 2026 agency-licence amendment found. Nothing new beyond K10.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Act 256/2001, with the last big amendment in 2017. Operators (mostly municipalities, also parishes) must hold written grave leases and keep a cemetery book. Sources describe paper card files as a risk. A Feb 2026 qualification standard expects knowledge of cemetery-book software. No commercial software found by search. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Associations must file annual accounts in the public register (§ 21a Accounting Act; fine up to CZK 100,000; repeated failure can lead to dissolution proceedings). Public-collection law amended by 239/2024 Sb. from 1 Jan 2025. Public access to the beneficial-owner register (ESM) was closed in Dec 2025. Halal and kosher supervision: nothing found. Generic accounting competes. Logged as weak.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi rules were last changed in 2020 (Act 115/2020 Sb., evidence sticker, driver permit). No 2026 amendment found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: ČNB licence (Act 277/2013 Sb.), premises notified electronically via REGIS, ČNB statement RS2020-11 on records and reporting, FAÚ reports within 5 days. Few operators (number unverified). Market traders: EET 2.0 is covered by K01 and K13. Money changers logged as weak.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Tattoo and body-care: from 1 Jan 2026 operators only notify the health authority (no operating-rules approval); this is deregulation and no deadline for existing operators was found. Driving schools: no 2026 filing change found; a 2026 digital-licence change only affects learners. Nurseries: K05. Hunting: K16. Small food producers: new candidates below, wine growers and breweries (breweries covered by existing customs guidance).

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Act 311/2006: distributors registered with Customs (20M CZK deposit), buy only from registered distributors, monthly electronic report within 20 days; owners of dispensing units with tanks over 5 m3 must keep a daily dispensing record for 3 years. No 2026 change found. Public EV chargers became legally regulated measuring instruments on 1 Jan 2026 (see candidate). Otherwise nothing new beyond the regime already served by fuel-station vendors.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Only MZe statistical return Obil (MZe) 7-02, now half-yearly from 2026, aimed at millers/bakers buying over 999 t and maltsters over 499 t, so not small firms. Nothing found for small grain buyers or warehouses. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: eRecept, eNeschopenka and insurer billing are state systems with established clinic software; GP complaints are about workload, not a missing product. Dental and vet X-ray registrants (SÚJB) found as a niche (see candidate). Nothing else new.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacies file an annual narcotics report to SÚKL by end Feb (2,449 pharmacies and 201 other dispensers in 2026; only 34 late, 33 fixed after reminder), and SUKL ran 382 inspections in 2025 under Act 167/1998 and precursor Act 272/2013. High compliance and pharmacy software suggest a weak gap. No new 2026 duty found.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Proposed amendment to the employment act: responsible person on a 20h/week contract, new licence-withdrawal grounds (2 years inactivity, missing insolvency insurance proof); adoption unconfirmed. Foreign-worker onboarding must go through JMHZ/REGZEC from 1 Apr 2026 (see candidate). Security agencies not searched separately.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Construction waste handled by Decree 273/2021 and Act 541/2020 (already K11 rejected). Mining-waste plans go to the district mining office every 5 years, a niche. No local-content type reports exist. Nothing new beyond K11/K12.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: AML Act 253/2008 amended by 107/2024 Sb. (from 1 May 2024): insolvency/restructuring administrators and precious-stone dealers newly obliged; contact person to FAU required since end 2024 (fine up to 10M CZK); 10-year retention; unreported suspicious deal up to 5M CZK. EU AMLR (2024/1624) applies from Jul 2027 (own knowledge, unverified here). One candidate listed.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Current duties: domovní kniha for foreigners kept 6 years, UbyPort report within 3 working days, evidenční kniha plus municipal poplatek z pobytu (fines up to 500,000 CZK). eTurista amendment (central register, registration number per unit, 24h guest reporting, fine up to 100,000 CZK in the 2025 draft) was still not finally adopted as of 11 Jun 2026; launch dates slipped repeatedly. Strongest new lead of this pass.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: EUDR: sources conflict on small-firm dates (30 Dec 2026 for medium/large, 30 Jun 2027 for micro/small; one source says timber applies from Dec 2026 regardless of size). Downstream traders do not file their own DDS once the first operator has. K02 already covers forest managers. Food and fish importers not searched.

coverage.found: Dental, veterinary X-ray and bone densitometers need SUJB registration since 2017, application A1, radiation-protection person required. No recurring filing found, mostly a one-off plus internal quality records. See weak candidate.

coverage.category: 32 Municipal fees and waste/EPR duties on small producers and sellers (packaging, electronics, batteries, tyres)
coverage.found: PPWR (EU 2025/40) applies from 12 Aug 2026, most concrete duties from 2028-2030, national penalties due by 12 Feb 2027; the Czech adaptation law is not confirmed. Czech packaging law: persons placing packaging on the market register in the MŽP Seznam osob within 60 days, with an 800 Kč fee and an annual evidence fee due by 15 Feb. A contract with EKO-KOM removes the duty. A de-minimis exemption exists for up to 300 kg packaging and up to 4.5M Kč turnover (old ePravo article, unverified). Act 542/2020 (EPR for electronics, batteries, tyres): ČOI found violations in 202 of 458 checks in Q1 2023, mainly missing disclosure of recycling cost at sale. A battery-law amendment, sněmovní tisk 58, is awaiting a first reading. Municipal local fees were not searched.

coverage.category: 33 Excise duty on small producers other than distilleries and wine: minibreweries, cider, mead, spirit bottlers, tobacco or hemp sellers

The excise returns use the electronic formats in Decree 451/2025 Sb. (annex 32 covers beer records). I found no brewery software, so the state's own shortcut makes a paper or Excel workflow adequate. Not checked: number of minibreweries, the reduced rate for small brewers, cider and mead makers, hemp sellers.

coverage.category: 36 New laws 2024-2027 hitting small operators: whistleblowing (Act 171/2023), accessibility (Act 424/2023), beneficial-owner register
coverage.found: Whistleblowing: internal channel required for 50+ employees since 15 Dec 2023, fine up to 1M Kč (secondary sources). Accessibility: Act 424/2023 applies to e-shops from 28 Jun 2025, ČOI supervises, fines up to 10M Kč, and the microenterprise exemption is described inconsistently across sources. Beneficial owners: associations not in a public register must file manually via justice.cz, and one blog cites fines up to 500,000 Kč. A bank glossary says SVJ are exempt (unverified). All three are generic compliance workflows with many consultants and website audit tools. Not checked: named vendors, the precise exemption text.

result.competitor: Free state filing channels already exist: the eAgri/Portál farmáře Registr vinic (built by CCV Informační systémy) and the SZPI portal for declarations and wine classification. They cover filing only, not the cellar books. In six Czech and English searches I found no Czech winery evidence-book software, only foreign tools (vintrace, InnoVint, Vintners Advantage, Vinsight, and the Slovenian EVINAR). It is possible that Czech ERP add-ons or small local vendors exist and are poorly indexed. That remains unverified.
result.duty: Act 321/2004 Sb. and decree 88/2017 Sb. § 13 (amended by 305/2023 Sb.), which replaced 323/2004 Sb. (the transition ended 31 Jul 2017). Evidence books follow Annexes 12-26: grape harvest and intake, purchase slips, processing and output by quality class, sucrose and enrichment, monthly wine stocks, and per-vessel stock and treatment cards. Producers under 500 hl a year may use the combined Annex 23/24. The decree explicitly allows electronic books if software makes each entry irreversible and records who made it, so the claim's doubt on this point is resolved. Deadlines for most books follow the directly applicable EU rules. Reg. 436/2009 has been replaced, I believe by Delegated Reg. 2018/273 and Implementing Reg. 2018/274, but I did not confirm this in the session. For bulk wine, entries are due by the next working day and monthly stocks by the 3rd working day. Declarations: harvest by 15 Jan (only growers who sell grapes or must), production and stocks (2025 calendar: stocks as of 31 Jul due by 10 Sep), and Wine Fund levy reports. These go through the free eAgri/Portál farmáře Registr vinic or the SZPI portal. SZPI supervises, and the NSS ruling upholds fines for incomplete records. I did not check fine amounts or the 2026 dates.
result.market: 2,236 registered wine producers under § 11 of Act 321/2004, plus 596 bulk-wine sellers under § 16b (MZe information-request response, 2021). 13,732 growers with planted vineyards at 31 Dec 2022 (Česká spořitelna, using ÚKZÚZ data), and 16,541 growers in the ČSÚ Vinice 2020 survey. Most are very small, many of them hobby growers.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Act 321/2004 Sb. and its implementing decree 88/2017 Sb. (amended by 305/2023; it replaced 323/2004) require evidence books in Annexes 12-26: intake, processing, monthly stocks, per-vessel cards, and a simplified Annex 23/24 for producers under 500 hl. The decree explicitly allows electronic books if every entry is irreversible and names who made it. Wineries also file harvest, production and stock declarations through free eAgri/Portál farmáře and SZPI portals, and NSS case law upholds fines for late or incomplete entries. In six Czech searches I found no Czech vendor, only foreign tools. A niche of about 2,200 registered producers, many of them hobby-sized, limits willingness to pay. A low-cost subscription that prints the books and pre-fills the declarations is plausible.
